title: Characterisation of social media conversations on syphilis: an unobtrusive observational study
screen_reason: Content analysis of a systematic 10% sample of 111,388 English-language 2019 tweets containing 'syphilis'. All tweets categorised as a 'medical resource' (n=1762) were assessed by an infectious disease registrar for clinical accuracy, yielding a stated share of items judged medically incorrect (240/1762, 14%). This is an item-level share with a denominator, judged for truth/falsity against expert verification, so it is CONTENT rather than QUALITY.

estimates.measure_type: % of syphilis 'medical resource' tweets judged medically incorrect by an infectious disease registrar
estimates.value_raw: 240/1762 (14%) medically incorrect; 1484/1762 (84%) medically correct; 38/1762 (2%) not judgeable (exact share of incorrect = 13.6%)
estimates.denominator: 1,762 tweets categorised as a 'medical resource' within a systematic 10% sample (n=11,113 after removal of 25 foreign-language tweets) of the 111,388 English-language tweets containing 'syphilis' posted in 2019
estimates.definition: A medical-resource tweet whose text, still images/videos and embedded links were reviewed by an infectious disease registrar and 'deemed to be medically incorrect'
estimates.misinfo_def: No formal definition of misinformation; the operational criterion is 'whether they were medically correct or incorrect', with the discussion framing these as 'Incorrect medical information'
estimates.source_quote: Of 1762 tweets (16%) categorised as a medical resource, 1484 (84%) were medically correct and 240 (14%) were medically incorrect; for 38 (2%), medical accuracy could not be judged from the information posted.
estimates.page_loc: Abstract, Results (p. 1); the same figures appear in Results p. 2 and Fig. 1b
estimates.ground_truth_detail: One researcher (AD) classified all sampled tweets into content categories using a two-round approach, with a scheme modified from Chew et al.; all tweets in the medical-resource category were then reviewed by a single infectious disease registrar (AF) for medical correctness. No inter-rater reliability statistic is reported, and no external fact-check or guideline standard is named.
estimates.moderator_quote: All tweets assigned to the category of medical resource were reviewed by an infectious disease registrar (AF) to determine whether they were medically correct or incorrect. The content of the text, any associated still images or videos and links provided within each tweet were considered in the assessment.
estimates.notes: Two judgement calls for an adjudicator. (1) Denominator: the 14% is a share of medical-resource tweets ONLY (1,762), not of all syphilis tweets sampled (11,113); the paper never states a false-content share of the full corpus, so no such row is created. I coded denom_selection=curated because the denominator is a purposively defined content sub-category rather than the natural keyword corpus; an adjudicator could defensibly leave it "". (2) value_pct uses the paper's verbatim 14%; the exact part/whole share from the verbatim counts is 240/1762 = 13.6%.

missed_or_uncertain: Not extracted: (a) 'only 13% of all tweets presented medically accurate information' - the numerator is CORRECT information, not misinformation, so it is not a prevalence-of-misinformation estimate (its complement would be a computed complement, barred by R8, and would also fold in the 84% of the corpus never assessed for accuracy). (b) The content-category shares (joke 5370/11,113 = 48%, public conversation 23%, medical resource 16%, spam 4%, etc.) are topic/genre categories, not veracity judgements. (c) The 2% (38 tweets) whose accuracy could not be determined is an indeterminate category, not a misinformation share. (d) Engagement ratios (personal experience approx. 19:1, medical resource approx. 7:1) are engagement, not misinformation shares. (e) Figures cited from other papers (Swetland et al. 74.4% of 358 tweets correct; other groups' 41-80% information-source shares; Chew 8% and Gabarron 10% jokes) are barred by R8 as figures the paper cites from elsewhere.

rob.design: Unobtrusive observational content analysis. Frame: every English-language tweet containing 'syphilis' posted 1 Jan - 31 Dec 2019, obtained from TrackMyHashtag on 8 Sep 2020, retweets excluded (N=111,388 tweets by 69,921 authors). A 10% systematic sample (every 10th tweet chronologically, chosen 'to avoid selection bias') gave n=11,113 after removing 25 foreign-language tweets. Categorisation into 10 content categories by a single researcher (AD) in two rounds, accessing the tweet online in thread context when needed; medical accuracy of the medical-resource category rated by a single infectious disease registrar (AF). No inter-rater reliability, no double-coding, no response rate applicable. Monthly tweet counts compared by Poisson regression. Ethics review not required (public data).
rob.item6_quote: All tweets assigned to the category of medical resource were reviewed by an infectious disease registrar (AF) to determine whether they were medically correct or incorrect.
rob.item10_quote: Of the 1762 tweets categorised as medical resource, 1484 tweets (84%) were judged to be medically correct, whereas 240 tweets (14%) were deemed to be medically incorrect; for 38 tweets (2%), it was not possible to determine medical accuracy (Fig. 1b).
